Commentary.Commentary: The hosts would be disappointed they couldn't wrap the Indians up earlier. Kind of like a taste of what the visitors felt when the home side was batting yesterday and Curran somewhat took the game away from them. A handful of overs left in the day, and the Indians will want to scalp a wicket or two before Stumps. The action will begin again quickly, stay tuned!

India were motoring along comfortably when Virat Kohli and Cheteshwar Pujara were batting, but once their 92-run stand was broken by Sam Curran, dismissing the former, things went rather awry for them. A few wickets fell in quick succession and then Moeen Ali came in to take the tail by storm. Pujara was running out of partners, but those last two stands - the first with Ishat Sharma worth 32, and the second with Jasprit Bumrah consisting of 46 - changed everything. Pujara ended up scoring a well-deserving unbeaten ton and giving England something to think about.

What a Test match! Just when you think it's over something different seems to put itself on display. India were on the brink of ending up in a position of weakness, but Cheteshwar Pujara's heroics have helped his side not only take the lead, but also be in a decent position, as the day is about to finish.

OUT! And he does it on the first one. This is a good ball. Hits the deck hard and it rises sharply on Bumrah. He has no idea about it, tries to awkwardly defend it but it goes off his gloves and pops up behind to Alastair Cook at first slip, who takes a dolly. Vital partnership of 46 comes to an end, as India are bowled out and LEAD BY 27 RUNS!
Around the off stump, Bumrah once again blocks. Two more opportunities for Broad to get rid of Bumrah.
Rock Solid. Jasprit Bumrah is showing good technique while playing. He gets right behind the line and defends it down the track.
Seems Anderson's been given the nod to bowl. Could be on soon. He's asking Joe Root from which end he should come on to bowl.
On a length, rising off the surface a touch, it is kept out.
Back of a length on the fifth stump line, Bumrah without any foot movement, tries getting some wood on leather, but his effort goes in vain.
Too far down the leg side, Pujara can't connect. Only way it seems they can keep him off strike.
Back of a length seaming in on middle and leg, blocked back down the track safely.
Shaping down leg from a length, an attempted flick misses completely.
Full toss outside off, sliced behind point. The run was there for the taking, but Pujara refused.

Partnership moves to 46 with this. Cheteshwar Pujara is batting cleverly here. Just has to find the gap, like he has here, and he's bound to get two. Flicks it through mid-wicket neatly and is back to face Curran.
Going away from around off, on a good length, Che has a tame poke at it from inside the line and gets beaten.
And this stand continues. Pujara once again does ever so well to keep the strike with him. Places it behind point and collects a run. The lead is of 25 now.
Big swing and an even bigger miss from Pujara. Full and outside off, he looks to clear The Rose Bowl by launching it big downtown. Misses the ball altogether.
Nicely done. It's short again but some width is on offer this time. So, Pujara hangs back and cuts it down to third man. No run taken though.
Still on the shorter side, Pujara goes deep inside the crease and blocks.
Short of a good length in line of the stumps, guarded out from the back foot.
Maintains the tight line as he bowls it on off, Cheteshwar remains rooted in the crease and blocks it back down the track.
Does that, but the line is too straight. Bumrah works it down gently on the leg side.
Curran has to make Bumrah play. No point bowling like this. Hurls it outside and the keeper takes it as the batsman leaves it alone.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Length delivery in the off stump channel, keeps on going away with the angle, Jasprit with an easy leave.
Full again, attacking the stumps on this occasion, Bumrah with surety blocks it out by bringing down a straight bat.
Fired well across the batsman, Bumrah doesn't move an inch. Doesn't have to, really. Just watches the ball and lets it go.
Sam Curran returns.
Just ahead of a length, close to off, run down towards point. Wants the run but Moeen Ali gets to it quickly, stopping the batsmen from achieving their goal.
On the fuller side of things once more, Che blocks it confidently.

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! This is incredible batting from the Indian no.3. It's full and outside off. Pujara nicely leans into the shot and crisply drives it through the covers for a boundary. The chasing fielder can do nothing about it.

FOUR! That is a terrific shot. Brute force and raw power from Cheteshwar Pujara. Haven't seen this side of him in a long time. He's expecting the ball to be full, so he uses the depth of the crease to get under the ball and lifts it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Full and fired just outside off, drilled right at the man at deep mid off.
Cutting back in from a good length, some extra bounce on offer, raps Pujara high on the thigh pad as he misses his shot.
The second new ball has been taken.
Well done, Pujara. He's farming the strike smartly. Plays it on the leg side and gets to the other end.
Pushes it gently to mid off. Dot ball.

FOUR! Pujara taking the attack to the English bowling attack. Once again makes good use of his feet to get close to the pitch and lofts it over Joe Root's head at deep mid off. The English skipper tries chasing it down but can't keep it inside the rope.
Some decent air on this one, outside the line of off stump, blocked.
Gives the charge to this tossed up delivery well outside off and drills it straight to extra cover.
Loopy leg break around off, full in length, Cheteshwar kneels down to sweep but can't make any sort of connection.
Adil Rashid is on again.
Just ahead of a length, close to off, Jasprit meets it with the full face of the bat.
He was expecting this. Waits for it, swivels and pulls it towards fine leg for one.
Full ball tailing back in, flicked comfortably down towards fine leg. The placement is good which will earn the batsman a couple.
Fraction straight in line, turned away on the leg side for nothing.

Good save from Sam Curran. Nice effort. Broad errs in line and bowls it way wide down the leg side, Pujara misses the tickle and so does Buttler. The ball is racing away to the fine leg fence but Curran out in the deep moves to his right and pulls it inches inside the rope. Two byes taken.
Close. Could have just as easily dragged it back on. Bumrah attempts to defend this fullish ball on off stump and gets an inside edge past the leg pole, down to fine leg. One run to the scoreboard.
Swinging back in from around the wicket, full in length, it's clipped behind square on the leg side. One run taken to end the over.
Full in length on middle and leg, flicked through the gap in the leg side for a single.
Wide! Consecutive wides. That's a rare sight. Curran once again fires it full and too far outside off, the umpire raises his arms sideways.
Wide! Too far outside off, across the tramline, wide called by the umpire.
Short of a good length outside off, run down to gully for no run.
Good length delivery on the off stick, blocked.
And INDIA TAKE THE LEAD BY 1 RUN! Pujara pulls this away through mid-wicket for a couple and puts his team ahead of England.
Too far outside off, Pujara goes after it but misses.

The full inswinger from Broad, Jasprit Bumrah does extremely well to keep this out. Flicks it down towards fine leg and obviously, takes no run. Survives the over with style. Pujara will be on strike for the next one.
Hurled a little too far outside off, no way Bumrah will fiddle with that one. Easy leave for him to make.
Too straight in line, on a back of a length, it's tapped down in front of short leg.
Banged in short, Jasprit takes the pull on, but the bounce gets too big on him and he can't connect.
Just outside off, on a good length, Bumrah covers the line and lets it be. Judged that one quite well.
Length ball aiming the top of off stump, Bumrah stands firm and blocks it under his nose.
Stuart Broad is called back into the attack. Three slips and a short leg in place for him.
Clever from Sam. Very clever. Bowls it down the leg side. Pujara tries flicking it but cannot get bat to ball. England have six balls to get Jasprit out.

FOUR! On a good length outside off, Pujara stays back and drives it powerfully through covers. Beats the infield and the ball runs away.  That is a shot of a man past the 3-figure mark. The deficit now is just 1. Can he though get a run in the next ball?
Fuller this time on middle and leg, flicked off his pads to the man at mid-wicket.
Back of a length on off, Pujara pulls it through mid-wicket for nothing.
Short ball on the leg side, Che pulls it to deep square leg. Does not take the run.
Full and around off, Pujara drives it to mid off.
Good from Bumrah. Googly coming in, Bumrah plays it with a straight bat.
Comes down again and hits this to mid on for one.
FOUR! Well played and nicely timed. Pujara plays this one very well as he uses his feet and flicks this through mid-wicket. No fielder there and the ball meets the ropes.
Pushed to cover for the man to collect it.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Bumrah survives and survives well. Guides this ball to third man and takes just a run.
Full and straight, no turn on this outside off, Pujara kneels down to paddle sweep it but misses as the ball goes under his bat.
The batsman dances down the track but decides to defend it.
Short ball, pulled away on the leg side for no run.
Pujara stays inside the crease and turns it away on the leg side.
Well done, Jasprit. That's well placed and the running between the wickets matches it. Works this through short fine leg and takes three.
Hangs back inside the crease and keeps it out.

100 for Pujara! His first in England, 15th overall in Tests. What a knock this has been. A real show of grit and determination from him. Ali gives this air in line of the stumps, Pujara charges down and lofts it over his head. The ball does not go all the way but they take the second run. He removes his helmet and soaks in all the applause.

NOT OUT! Impact outside off and he was offering a shot. Ali bowls this way outside off, Pujara gets forward, keeps his bat and pad close trying to block it. The ball hits his pad and bunts down. The fielding side has a tame appeal but the umpire stays put. Moeen has a chat with his partner and they take it up. The umpire thinks he was offering a shot, so the impact matters here. It was outside off which puts the argument to bed.
LBW review! England have opted for it against Pujara, but he seems to be safe. Let's see...
Nicely done! Full and outside off, Pujara sweeps this one towards square leg. The man in the deep dives to keep it to two. Moves to 99 now.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Hammers this to deep mid-wicket and he doesn't take the single.
Full and on the pads, flicked to the man at square leg.
Gets the single! Taps this with soft hands towards mid off and hares to complete the run.
Rashid sees Pujara charging down and darts this wide outside off. Pujara does not offer any shot and drags his foot back.
Stays back and cuts it to the man at point.
Another one outside off, left alone.
Leg spinner around off, Pujara watches it go through.
Short ball on middle and off, Pujara rocks back and pulls it towards cow corner. Finds the man and does not take the run.
Jasprit Bumrah is the last man in.

OUT! Got 'em! 5th Test 5-fer for Moeen Ali. He's steamrolled the tail here. Gets another to his name. Lands it around off and it spins back in with some extra bounce. Goes off the bat apparently, then the pad and into the hands of Alastair Cook at short leg. The finger goes up in response to the appeal but Ishant is upset. He indicates there's no bat but Snicko detects a feather. He's gone. End of a useful knock from him though.
Works it off his pads but no run taken.
Stays inside the crease and keeps it out.
FOUR! Gets low early to this tossed up one and sweeps it behind square leg. Through the gap and that will be a boundary.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Pujara dances down and pushes it through extra cover. Thinks long and hard about taking the run, then eventually takes it midway through the track.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Gives this too much air in line of the stumps, Sharma bunts it down.
Floated ball on middle and leg, Sharma comes down and looks to flick this away. Gets an inside edge towards short leg.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Steps out and hits this ball through covers to rotate strike.
And gives the strike to Pujara in the very first ball. Goes back and punches this ball to the off side to get to the other end.
Can't find the gap and will not take strike for the next over. Works this off his pads but finds the man at square leg.
FOUR! Shot! Pujara moves to 94. What a confidence booster this will be for him if he gets to a 100 in England. Comes down the wicket again and chips this over mid-wicket all the way to the fence.
Loopy ball outside off, Che dances down the track and hits this to the off side.
CP has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Loopy ball outside off, Pujara looks to sweep this but gets hit on his pads. Another appeal which dies down.
Reads the off spinner and brings his pads out to get hit outside off.
Ishant has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Keeps low, Sharma stonewalls it.

An appeal for LBW has been turned down. Rashid bowls this outside off, Sharma looks to bring out the sweep again. He misses it this time and gets hit on his pads. They appeal but he was struck outside the line of the stumps.
Tossed up ball outside off, Sharma drives it to covers.
Full of authority. Swipes this through square leg and gets two runs for it.
Adil Rashid is called into the attack.
Gets to the pitch of the ball and milks it through mid on. With the confidence Sharma is showing, they take the run.
Well played. Googly on middle and leg, Sharma gets his bat down in time and blocks it well.
Stands tall and punches the ball through covers to give his partner the strike.

FOUR! Finally a boundary for Pujara. He does not play that much of white-ball cricket, but is trying his best to score as much as he can, as fast as he can. Waits for the ball to come to him and cuts it late towards third man for a boundary.
Off spinner on off, Pujara rocks back and plays it onto the ground.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Ali tosses this one outside off, Pujara charges down the wicket and bunts it.
Length ball around off, Sharma plays it with the full face.
Short ball down leg, Che pulls it with ease to deep backward square leg and this time gets off strike.
Another short ball, Pujara controls this pull to deep backward square leg but does not bother running.
Bangs this one short down the leg side. Pujara does not bother playing at this.
Short ploy from Anderson. Pujara connects but does not run.
Short ball down leg, Pujara pulls it to deep square leg. A loud shout for NO to his partner.
Sharma looks confident. Gets behind this ball and plays it onto the ground.
Off spinner outside off, Sharma bunts it down.
Strange that Pujara is giving the strike to Sharma. Pulls this ball through square leg to get to the other end.

Now we know why! Doesn't go all the way but a very good-looking shot from Ishant. Ali gives this air outside off, Sharma uses his feet and lofts it over mid off. The ball stops near the rope and the batsmen come back for the third run.
Surprise. Pujara takes the run. Why? Let's find out. Plays this with soft hands to mid off and quickly hares to the other end. The fielder there, has a shy at the stumps but misses.
Looks to play it delicately past third man but hits it to the man stationed there.
Sharma survives. Outside off, no trouble for the batsman who leaves it alone.
Gets what he wants. Milks this through mid-wicket and gives Ishant the strike to face the last ball.
Wide down the leg side, Che leaves it alone.
Full and on middle and leg, Che hits it to mid on.
Shot! Another short ball outside off, Pujara stays inside and cuts it past backward point for a brace.

Nasty! This is the second time Che has got hit on the helmet. This one though is not as bad as the previous one. Anderson digs it short down leg, Pujara sways away from it but the ball goes on to hit the back of his helmet. No damage done though.
Lovely from Sharma. Gets forward and stonewalls this ball into the ground.
Gets behind the ball and blocks this down.
FOUR! Shot! This is good from Sharma. Brings out the broom again, reaches for the ball from outside off and finds the fence through square leg.
Ishant has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Positive intent from Sharma. Gets on one knee and sweeps the ball hard. Unfortunately for him, he finds the man at short leg.
No hat-trick for Moeen! An umbrella field for Sharma. The offie tosses this one up outside off, Sharma gets ahead and bunts it down.
Good from England. They don't concede the single which means Sharma will face the hat-trick ball. Length ball outside off, Pujara looks to guide this one through the cordon but finds Moeen at gully.
Length ball outside off, Pujara looks to cut it hard but the ball goes past his bat.
Short ball outside off, Pujara looks to pull it but cannot make contact. England will now look to keep Pujara on strike for the next two balls. The field is up.
Short ball on middle and leg, Pujara pulls it through mid-wicket but refuses to take the run.
Still not bothered to play at this. Sees the ball outside off and lets it be.
Length ball outside off, Che leaves it alone. It will be interesting to see how Pujara plays with the tail here.
Ishant Sharma comes out to bat.

OUT! Two in two for Moeen Ali. What a spell from the bearded man. Comes in from over the wicket and lands this on middle and off, Shami goes back and looks to play at it with a straight bat. The ball does just enough to go and hit the off pole. India have lost their last 6 wickets for 53 runs and Moeen will be on a hat-trick in his next over.
Mohammed Shami is the new man in.

OUT! Poor from Ashwin. Not the shot he should have played and it causes his downfall. Moeen gives this air outside off, Ashwin premeditates, gets on one knee and looks to reverse sweep this one. The ball hits the bottom of the bat, bounces and goes on to hit the timber. India far from reaching the hosts' total, still trail by 51 runs.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Off spinner outside off, Ashwin goes for the drive but fails to put bat to ball.
Goes back and punches this ball off his back foot to the off side.
Short and wide, Pujara square cuts this to give Ashwin the strike.
Pujara has played it towards mid-wicket. They pick up a single.
The ball is way wide on the leg side but the batsman still goes after it. The batsmen have run through for a single. Byes signalled by the umpire.
Fuller one for Ashwin who drives it to mid off.
Outside off, Pujara cuts it past point to get to the other end.
Another one banged in short. Che ducks in time to let it pass.
Anderson is going to bowl this way. Going to give some chin music to these batsmen. Digs one in on middle and leg, Pujara sways away from this.
Pujara gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it through covers. They pick up a single.
Che rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Ashwin is off the mark. Plays this with soft hands towards mid off and gets to the other end.
Ravichandran Ashwin walks out to the middle.

OUT! Outstanding catch! England ripping the Indian lower middle order and have not only got themselves back into this game, but also in a comfortable zone. India's tail are not that strong as that of the hosts and they will hope they wrap this up ASAP. Moeen floats this around off, Pandya comes ahead and looks to milk this away. Root with a perfect field set has positioned himself at short mid-wicket. He dives to his left and takes a good low catch.
Another one given air, Pandya gets behind the ball and plays it with a straight bat.
Tosses this ball outside off, CP uses his feet and drives it towards extra cover for a run.
Shuffles across and milks this through mid-wicket for a single.
Nice! Back of a length ball outside off, Pujara rocks back and cuts this uppishly over backward point for a brace.
Full again outside off, Pujara hits it towards cover-point.
Fuller this time in line of the stumps, Che plays it onto the ground.
On a good length again outside off, Pujara watches the ball go through to the keeper.
Anderson comes in from over the wicket and lands it on a good length outside off, Che takes a step and drives it to mid off.
Comes ahead and hits this ball to the off side.
FOUR! 29 balls for Pant to get off the mark. Hardik Pandya, 'Hold my Beer'. Gets on one knee to this floated ball and sweeps this through mid-wicket for a rocketing boundary.
Tosses it up around off, Pandya gets forward and bunts it down.

We are back for the last session of the day. Expect India to be more positive now. They will take a lead of 50-odd runs with both hands. Hardik Pandya joins Cheteshwar Pujara at the crease. Moeen Ali will continue his over.
... Day 2, Session 3...

So England have somewhat pulled things back in this afternoon session. Leaked 81 runs but picked up three vital wickets, of Kohli, Rahane (whose dismissal was questionable) and at the stroke of the break, Pant. Pujara is still standing out there, holding one end. The coming batsmen will have to support him well as India still trail by 65 runs. Ben Stokes and Sam Curran made all the difference with their fiery and attacking spells, picking up a wicket each and Moeen Ali got the third one on what was the last over of the session. These last two hours will determine who will hold the advantage in this Test match. It should be a good one. Don't go anywhere, it will begin shortly...

OUT! Pant is gone for a duck, despite facing 29 deliveries! Unbelievable. He hasn't looked as assured as he did in the previous game and eventually, Moeen Ali ends his misery. Tosses this up on leg, it spins and strikes Pant on the front pad as he misses his defense. A loud shout goes up and so does the finger. No reviews left so there's nothing he can do. Was gone anyway, the replays confirmed that. A dead duck. That will be TEA ON DAY 2!
Makes use of the feet to get close to the ball and keeps it out.
Looped up outside off, driven to the man at cover.
Moeen Ali back on to bowl the last over before Tea.
He is not off the mark yet. Pant shoulders arms to let it through and Buttler fumbles. The batsmen take a bye to end the over.
From around the wicket, it's in the channel outside off, Pant plays away from his body and gets beaten.
Short and wide, cut away square on the off side for a single.
Not threatening the batsman at all as the bowler bowls it outside off, arms are shouldered.
Length delivery, close to off, safely pushed away.
Short of a good length outside off, blocked off the back foot.
A play and a miss as Pant throws his bat at it only to miss. Pant is yet to get off the mark.
In the off stump channel, Pant doesn't flirt with it.
Back of a length outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Stifled shout but Stokes pulls out of it immediately. Cutting back in from a good length, Pujara is caught high on the thigh pads. Rightly, the umpire doesn't bother it.
FOUR! Two in two for Che. A bit too straight in line and Pujara doesn't think twice to put it away. Tickles it fine down the leg side, past a diving Jos Buttler for consecutive boundaries.

FOUR! A boundary after ages. Oh that's just beautiful. Beautiful. Could watch that all day long. Pujara nicely leans forward to this full length ball and drives it through the covers to find the fence. No stopping that.
Rishabh chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Too far outside off from around the wicket, Pant shoulders arms to it.
A rare bad ball and Pujara gets a run off it. Places it behind point and jogs over to the other end.
Not giving Pujara any room as Anderson pitches it quite close to off, the batsman can only defend it out.
Hurled wider of off than he would have liked, no way Che plays at it.
Aiming the top of off stump, on a good length, Cheteshwar Pujara meets it with a straight bat.
The batsman plays it with an angled bat and guides it to short third man.
Wide of off again, left alone for the keeper.
Short ball outside the line of off stump, evaded without much problem.
Fullish in length and making the batsman play, Pant is half-forward to defend.
Shaping away late from Pant, who hangs his bat out to play at it. Could have edged it, needs to be careful.
Heavy inward movement for Ben Stokes. Comes a long way in from outside off, Pujara does well to flick this through mid-wicket and get one.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Closer to off, on a good length, goes off the inside edge and thuds into the pads.
Coming in at first before seaming away, Pant makes a good leave.
Anderson is not happy with the shape of the ball. He shows it to the umpire who puts it through the 8-shaped gauge. Goes through just fine and he asks him to continue with it.
Bit of width offered outside off, Pujara gets this off the outer half down towards third man. One run collected.
In that off stump channel, it's left alone for the keeper to collect.
Full in length and on the pads, Pujara comes half-forward and clips it the man in front of square leg.
Stands inside his crease and hits this ball on the up towards mid on.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Comes in from round the wicket and serves it on a good length outside off, the ball nips back in but Rishabh shoulders his arms to it.
Fullish again on middle and leg, Pant plays it with a straight bat.
Full and outside off, Pant uses his feet and drives it to mid off.
The physio is out to have a look at Pujara. He seems to be fine, which is good to see. Going to need just a breather from the looks of things.

That was nasty! Ouch! Stokes brings out the short one and it's quite accurate. Aimed right at Pujara who takes the pull shot on. The bounce gets too big on him though and he cops a blow on the helmet. It flies behind point and the batsmen change ends. Stokes checks up on him as Che takes his helmet off.
Around the wicket to Pant, angling in on a length, the Indian keeper-batsman stays rooted in his crease and nudges it in front of square leg.
Length ball, it's run down to third man with an open face. Single taken.
Arms are shouldered to this length ball outside off. Again.
Does just that, but it's still not close enough. Cheteshwar ensures to cover the line and let it be.
Hawk Eye has gone down for the time being. Some technical issue probably. That means that there will be no DRS available till it's back up and running.
Watches the ball closely and lets it go past him as it's well away. Stokes needs to bring it closer to the off stick.
Keeps it outside off and on a length, Pujara covers the line and leaves.
James Anderson is back.
One more outside the line of off stump and another leave from the left-hander.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
No ball! Stokes oversteps as he hurls it outside off, so the umpire signals it as a no ball.
On the fuller side of things, attacking the stumps from around the wicket, Pant is comfortable as he meets the ball with his bat.
Closes the face and flicks this through the gap in the mid-wicket area. One run to the total.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, no shot offered.
Too full and too wide of off stump, Pujara is not going to bother himself with that.
Pant plants his front foot forward and blocks the full ball with a straight blade.
Angling down leg, Pujara looks to tickle it fine but misses. Buttler dives to his left and makes a half-stop. A bye is taken.
On the shorter side of the length, outside off, played away just wide of gully, but can't get it past the fielder.
Wide! Sam bangs it in short once more, but it's too short on this occasion. The umpire signals a wide.
Another bouncer, it's left alone.
Hits the deck hard and pounds it in short, angling into the batsman, Pujara ducks and evades.
Curran spears a yorker on off stump, Pujara crouches really low and keeps it at bay.
Stokes ends the over from around the wicket, bowls it outside off and makes it go away off the seam. Pant raises his bat and lets it pass. End of a successful over from Ben Stokes.
Rishabh Pant is next in.

OUT! Stokes gets the breakthrough. Take nothing away from him, that's a superb delivery, but that's possibly a no ball. Dicey call from the umpire. This will be one that will create a lot of chatter in the hours to follow. After a few outswingers, Big Ben brings this one in and gets some serious movement. Rahane attempts to block but is beaten completely and rapped on the front pad. A loud appeal goes up and the finger follows soon after. The batsman, after speaking with his partner, decides to use the DRS and it's taken upstairs. Replay rolls in and it checks for the front foot no ball first. It shows that Stokes very likely has his front foot over the line, but the TV umpire is heard saying he thinks it's fine. The rest, well, all three boxes are ticked and Rahane is out of here. He walks back disappointed.
Review time. Rahane looks to be dead plumb. What will happen here?
Works it off his pads on the leg side for no run.
Angling in first before straightening up off the deck, Rahane places himself perfectly behind the line and defends.
Back of a length outside off, blocked.
FOUR! Overpitched and that's gleefully put away. Well outside off, moving away, Rahane reaches out to it and caresses the drive through the gap in the covers. Finds the fence with ease.
Moves inside the line and works it away on the leg side.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Ooh! Venomous from Sam Curran. Some indecisiveness on Pujara's part too. Back of a length on middle, Pujara comes half-forward when he should be back and ends up getting it off the inside edge on the leg side. Close call. Lucky nothing drastic happened.
Behind a good length, close to the off stick, Pujara presents a defensive bat in response.
Stays behind the line and keeps it out without any problem.
Shaping back in on a bit of a shorter length, it's clipped down to fine leg for one.

Time for Drinks! A really interesting contest between bat and ball is going on at the moment. After the dismissal of Virat Kohli, there is a new zeal and intensity among the Englishmen. Stokes and Curran are in good rhythm and they are inducing false strokes as well. Rahane and Pujara have to be watchful.
Shortish delivery, Che hops back and tucks it towards mid-wicket.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Stokes is bending his back! Good length ball outside off, a lot of nibble in the air. Pujara keeps it out off the inner half of the bat.
Stokes slips this one down the leg side. It is short and has good pace on it but it is ill-directed. CP lets it go.
On a length outside off, left alone.
No ball! Stokes oversteps again, this time by a big margin! Fullish ball around off, kept out watchfully.

Dropped! A lot of activity is happening in the slip cordon. In the avenue of apprehension, shapes in a touch after landing. Rahane fishes at it and gets an outside edge behind. The ball flies towards Root at second slip. It is at a very low height as Joe dives to his right but the ball doesn't stick. It rolls towards third man and a run is taken. It was not an easy chance by any means. England are all over India at the moment.
Sharp bumper from Curran, Pujara just about manages to evade it.
Short of a good length well outside off, Rahane taps it down square on the off side and takes a brisk run.
Fires it on the stumps, quite full in length, pushed gently to mid on. Dot ball.
Back of a length, angling in on the hips, worked past square leg for one more.
Full and coming in from around off, Pujara brings a straight bat down in defense.
Angling in from around the wicket, outside off, Rahane dabs it with an open face behind point and crosses over.
This one is way outside off, ignored by Pujara.
In the same channel, Cheteshwar comes forward and dead-bats it.
Full again outside off, shaping away late. Che doesn't chase it.
Full ball outside off, driven to covers.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

FOUR! Another chance perhaps! On a fuller length around off, Pujara pushes at it and gets an outside edge. Buttler is a bit late to react, dives to his right but the ball just goes past him and beats Cook as well to reach the fence. The replays show that the ball was at a catchable height for the keeper but he was slow to take off. Stokes is making his presence felt.
No ball! Stokes oversteps straightaway! On a length around off, takes the inside edge of Pujara's bat and then dies down.
Ben Stokes to have a bowl now.
Full ball outside off, Rahane doesn't fall for the bait and lets it go.
Fullish ball around off, kept out watchfully.
The batsman has played it to the point region. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.

19th Test fifty for Cheteshwar Pujara! Good length ball, Che tucks it off the inner half through backward square leg for a run. He has been solid as a rock and deserves all the applause. Needs to continue in the same manner, especially after his captain getting dismissed.
On a length outside off, Rahane glides it past point for a run and gets off the mark.
Ajinkya Rahane comes out to bat.

OUT! England have sent the big fish packing! That dismissal will boost the morale of the Englishmen by leaps and bounds. On a length outside off, angled across, Kohli comes forward and does the mistake of playing away from his body. A fat outside edge results as the ball flies towards Alastair Cook at first slip. He gets low to his right and takes a very fine catch. The Indian skipper starts walking off immediately, showing good sportsmanship. In the previous innings, Cook had gone back too after Virat had taken a good low catch in the slip cordon. These kind of examples should be soaked in by the budding cricketers. India are behind by 104 runs.
Fullish ball around off, driven to mid on for a single.

Beaten all ends up! Tossed up delivery well outside off, drawing Kohli forward. He tries to cover the non-existent turn and the ball goes past the outside edge of his bat. Buttler takes the bails off but Virat hasn't dragged his back foot out.
Hangs back to a delivery which is on a flatter trajectory and blocks it nicely.
Pujara is nimble on his feet as he skips down the track and helps it through square leg for an easy run. Moves to 49 with that.
Floated outside off, Virat strokes it through covers for a single.
Slower through the air, Kohli comes forward and presents a water-tight defense.
FOUR! Hallmark of a really good player! Gets a fractionally overpitched delivery and pounces on it. Pujara leans ahead and drives it beautifully through extra cover for a delightful boundary.
Pitched up delivery, Che comes forward and dead-bats it.
Very full ball around the off stump channel, squeezed out to the cover region.
On a length outside off, Pujara hangs back and plays it with an angled bat to point.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

A huge appeal for an LBW falls on deaf ears! Curran starts from around the wicket and bowls a length ball around off. It comes in with the natural angle as it seems to have gone past Pujara's defense and brushes his pads. It lobs towards the slip cordon and falls down safely. The Englishmen appeal but the umpire turns it down. Root thinks about the review but doesn't go for it. There might have been an inside edge there as well, suggest the replays.
Sam Curran returns for a burst.
Spinning in from well outside off, Kohli shuffles a touch and defends it right under his eyes.

Deft from Pujara! Pushed quicker through the air outside off, Che dabs it late towards third man. Stokes gives it a chase and slides near the fence. Kohli calls his partner through for the third and makes the danger end safely.
Shorter in length, kept out watchfully.
Uses his feet to this one but is not quite to the pitch of it and hence defends it.
Floated outside off, Kohli leans forward and drives it to sweeper cover for a single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
On a length around off, cutting in. Pujara blocks it with his bat and pad close together.
Overpitched outside off, driven hard to sweeper cover for a single.
Nice inswinger from Broad. On a length outside off, coming in appreciably. Kohli covers his stumps and watches the ball go through to the keeper.
Full length ball attacking the stumps, pushed gently off the front foot towards mid on.
Good running! Straying on the pads this time, Kohli clips it through square leg and calls his partner through for a couple.
Pitched up ball around off, Kohli with a high elbow eases it to covers.
Easy pickings! Spinning down the leg side, Kohli tucks it away through the vacant fine leg region. Rashid gives it a chase and saves a run for his side.

FOUR! That could have been converted into an opportunity! Much better from Ali. After bowling 4 short balls, he bowls this one full outside off. Kohli is drawn into the drive and gets an outside edge. The ball goes through the gap between the keeper and Stokes at first slip and runs through to the fence. Should have been Buttler's to take, was quite close to him. Could prove costly for the home side.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Drifting in, too straight, clipped away smartly through square leg for a brace.
Shorter in length again, Che has no trouble in dealing with it off the back foot.
Pujara camps back and places the short ball towards square leg.
On a fullish length, shaping in nicely. Kohli gets on top of the bounce and defends it to covers. Brilliant over from Broad.
Peach! He bowled a similar ball in his previous over to Pujara. Lands it in the corridor of uncertainty and then gets it to straighten to go past the defense of the clueless Kohli.
Well bowled! That is the area that Broad needs to target, Kohli's off stump. Fuller in length around off, seams away a touch. Kohli pushes at it but gets beaten.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Anderson is suggesting something to Broad. They are probably discussing about whether they should bring the backward gully back in position.

FOUR! Sit back and enjoy! That was a mere push but the timing on that one was sensational. Fractionally overpitched on middle, Kohli, who is standing outside his crease, strokes it past Broad and through mid on to find the fence.
In the zone outside off, the Indian skipper allows it through.
Shouts of catch it but there was no bat involved! Turning in sharply, Pujara comes ahead and pads it away towards leg gully.
On a flatter trajectory, Che hangs back and works it towards square leg.
Shorter in length, Kohli camps back and works it with the spin to mid on for a quick run.
Allows the ball to come to him and drives it with the spin past the right side of the bowler for a single.
Slower through the air, spinning in, bunted down the pitch.
Full ball outside off, creamed to sweeper cover for a run.

FOUR! This time he is also watchful but with aggressive intent. Short and asking for trouble as it is well outside off. Pujara stands tall and cuts it through the point region to pick up his second boundary of the over.
Pujara is so watchful! Keeps his eyes on the incoming short of a length ball and makes an assured leave.
Short of a length outside off, punched sweetly off the back foot to the man at point.

That's a jaffa! Broad bowls this one with a slightly scrambled seam. It is coming in initially with the natural over the wicket angle but once it lands, it nips away to go past the forward push of Che. He had no clue about that.
The man at deep backward gully moves to third man. He is being moved finer.
FOUR! When you flash, flash hard! A pretty safe shot in the end. Short and there is width on offer. Pujara slaps it but gets it off the outer half over the slip cordon for a rocketing boundary.
Good length ball on off, cutting in with some appreciable bounce. Pujara hops and defends it to towards short mid-wicket. Shouts NO loudly to Kohli.
Shorter in length, allows enough time to Che to rock back and cut it through point for a run. He will retain the strike.
Drifting towards the pads, helped to square leg.
Pujara comes down the track to the loopy ball and defends it down.
Fuller in length, knocked down to mid on for an easy run.
That's the line and length to be bowling on this track. Tossed up on the rough patch outside off and it spins in sharply to go past the defense of Kohli and raps him on the pads.
Spinning into Kohli who leans ahead and taps it towards mid-wicket.
Moeen Ali to bowl from the other end.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

That was risky! These two have to work hard on their calling. Fullish ball outside off, Kohli taps it towards cover-point and calls Pujara through to which he agrees. The fielder picks up the ball and has a shy at the striker's end but misses as Cheteshwar has to dive in. Would have been safe though even if that hit but they need to be careful.
That one took off! On a length outside off, some extra bounce and away seam movement there as Kohli makes a watchful leave.

Well, the communication between Kohli and Pujara is not good when it comes to running between the wickets. Good length ball well outside off, Virat taps it towards point and takes off. He is egging his partner to respond to him but he tells him to go back. Well, the fielder was a bit deep so there was a run on offer.
On a length on middle and leg, tucked away nicely towards square leg.
We are back for the afternoon session. Cheteshwar Pujara and Virat Kohli to resume their innings. Stuart Broad to steam in with the ball first up after Lunch. Three slips in place. Here we go...
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

Remember, the pitch is easing out and and it is only going to become easier to bat with the ball becoming softer. India should be patient and play the way they are playing. England, on the other hand, will have to get things done themselves. Join us in a short while for the second session.

Stuart Broad and James Anderson were better with the ball today compared to last evening's four overs. They were pitching the ball up and were inviting the batsmen to drive. Broad bowling long spells was rewarded with a brace of wickets. The spinners have not got their hands on the ball much but we will see more of that post Lunch.

Good cricket overall. Some good bowling and equally smart batting. Clearly India on top at this point. They have seen off the new ball and have lost just their openers. Captain Kohli will be pleased with the way his side has shown application so far. KL Rahul and Shikhar Dhawan came out with positive intent. They were scoring at a healthy rate too. After the former's dismissal, the scoring went a tad slow. Rahul got out to a good ball but the southpaw threw his wicket away. Cheteshwar Pujara and Virat Kohli reduced the trail to 146 without further hiccups.
Good over from Moeen. Pujara and India can go into the break without more damage. Gets to the pitch of the ball and defends this ball. Lunch on Day 2.
Again! Not too far from the short leg fielder. Pujara looks to bunt this down but it lobs up to the on side. Falls safely though.
Cries of catch it but it is far from the short leg fielder. Pujara comes ahead to this tossed up ball and defends it. The ball lobs up but it is away from the short leg fielder.
Che has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Stays inside his crease and bunts this ball down.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Last over before Lunch. Meanwhile, Moeen Ali is called on for a bowl.
Another googly coming in after pitching, Pujara hits it through point to retain strike. 100 comes up for India. The 50-run stand is also up between the two. Good going from them.

What was that? Googly which pitched on the rough. Lucky for Pujara it didn't shoot up. Rashid serves this outside off, the ball pitches on a rough patch and keeps very low. Pujara does not offer any shot to it.
Misses his length and serves a juicy full toss outside off, Kohli drives it through extra cover for just a single.
Quicker one in line of the stumps, Kohli plays it with a straight bat.
Leg spinner outside off, Kohli shoulders his arms to it.
Tossed up ball around off, Virat drives it with soft hands to mid off.
Shot! Another back of a length ball outside off, Pujara transfers his weight to his back foot and punches the ball through covers. Does not go all the way but will get two for it.
Runs in from over the wicket and darts it around off, Pujara dead-bats it.
Full and outside off, Pujara watches the ball go through.
Che lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Back of a length ball down leg, Kohli hops and tucks it away to the on side for one.
On a good length on middle and off, Kohli gets ahead to block it but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Quicker and flatter outside off, Pujara lets it be.
Another googly from Rashid. It is shorter in length which allows Kohli to rock back and work it through mid-wicket for a single.
Slower through the air, pitched right up, eased off the front foot towards mid off.
Outside off, spinning away, left alone.

Poor from Anderson! Tossed up outside off, driven towards him as he fumbles. The batsmen scurry across for a quick run. Well, there is a wild throw from James too at the striker's end which allows them to take an overthrow.

Action straightaway! Slips in the googly first up, Kohli probably reads it and tries to flick it away with the spin but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball lobs and falls behind the vacant silly point region.
Time for spin. Adil Rashid to roll his arm over now. Can he strike before Lunch?
Kohli works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
The ball is down the leg side but the batsman still goes after it.
Short ball way outside off, Kohli leaves it alone.
Full on middle and leg, hit to mid on.
Keaton shouldn't be taken lightly. Bowls this on a back of a length down leg, Kohli misses his flick and gets hit on his thigh pad. They appeal but with no real intent.
On a good length outside off, Kohli defends it easily.
Keaton Jennings is called into the attack to have a shy.
Close! Full again on middle and off, Kohli leans ahead to drive but gets an inside edge to it. The ball goes past the leg stump towards fine leg for a run.
Full on middle and leg, Kohli gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Gets to the pitch of the ball and plays it into the ground.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
On a good length down the leg side, Kohli goes after it but cannot make any contact.

FOUR! On his way to 7000 runs! Shots like these, makes Kohli the player he is. Pitched up ball outside off, Kohli takes a step ahead and drives it through covers. The fielder dives near the ropes but cannot prevent the ball from reaching the fence.
Full again around off, Pujara drives it to mid off.
Pitched up ball outside off, Pujara waits for it and drives it in the gap through covers. The man from the circle runs after it and keeps it to two.
On a good length outside off, Pujara thinks of playing at it but withdraws at the last moment.
The ball is too wide on the off side for the batsman to make any contact.
VK works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.

FOUR! In the air... but safe! England will want that man at gully closer. Curran darts this full and way outside off, Kohli gets low and reaches for the ball. Opens the bat face at the last moment and slices it towards gully. Stokes there dives but the ball is away from him. The ball races to the boundary.
Anderson is getting the ball to move through the air. Gets this one into the batsman. Pujara covers his stumps and hits it towards the bowler.
Closer to the off pole, Che drives it to mid off.
On a good length, pitched up outside off, Pujara shoulders his arms to it as the ball moves away from him.
Gets the ball to shape away from Pujara who is happy to leave it alone.
Better from Anderson. Gets his line and length better on this occasion. Serves it full on middle and leg, Pujara gets it off the inner half through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
FOUR! Cut away and cut away nicely to the boundary. Short and wide outside off, Pujara rocks back and slaps this through point for a good looking boundary.
On a good length this time wide outside off, Kohli leaves it alone.
Sam is pitching it up but Kohli is not tempted to drive. Gets behind the ball and plays it with soft hands.
Full and on that fifth stump line, Kohli plays it into the ground with a full bat face.
Drags his length back on middle and leg, Pujara pulls it through mid-wicket for a run.
Gets to the pitch of the ball and bunts this down.
Full and outside off, left alone.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.

FOUR! Anderson gets the edge but it goes past the slip cordon and towards the boundary. Full and outside off, Kohli reaches for it and gets a fat edge to it. The ball flies past the third slip fielder and to the third man region to meet the fence. 6000 Test runs for Virat Kohli and he becomes the second fastest Indian to get there. Records are meant to be broken and Virat Kohli has a habit of getting his name into the record books. Like they say, 'Whaaaattaaaa plaaaaayyaaaa'!
Full and outside off, Kohli leaves it alone.
Pujara does what the fans wanted him to do. 'Give Kohli the strike and let him face Anderson'. Che plays this with soft hands towards cover-point and moves to the other end.
Comes in from over the wicket and lands this outside off. It moves away and Pujara points his bat skywards and lets it be.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for CP.
Played to the point region by Virat.

Leg side and Kohli will think he has missed out there. The only man on the leg side is the man at deep square leg. Sam bowls this on a good length on the pads, Kohli tries flicking it but cannot get bat to ball.
Full and outside off, Kohli shoulders his arms to it.
Uses his feet to perfection to get behind the ball and plays it into the ground.
Kohli lets this ball go outside his off stump.
Full outside off, Kohli hits it to the off side and shouts a loud NO. Remember, Kohli and Pujara are in the middle, the calling is going to be loud and clear.

Sweet! But not the best of timings. Broad serves it up in line of the stumps. Pujara gets bat to it and drives it down the ground along the turf. The mid off fielder hares towards the ball to keep it to two.
That ball has taken the inside edge of Che and thudded into his pads.
Full this time around off, Pujara stonewalls it.

FOUR! Streaky! Broad is making Pujara commit mistakes. Bowls this short and wide outside off. Pujara stays inside, opens the bat face and guides it uppishly over the cordon. The ball runs away to the fence. That was risky. Pujara needs to be careful.
Back of a length ball outside off, Kohli hits it through mid off to get off strike.

FOUR! Kohli cover drive! Two in two balls for India. One from Pujara and the other one from the skipper. Broad into his 8th over of the spell, pitches this up around off. Kohli who has just faced one ball before this goes ahead and drives it sweetly through covers. Nobody moves and Kohli is up and running.
FOUR! Shot! First for Pujara and a lovely one. Sam serves it up outside off. Pujara's eyes light up, he reaches for the ball and eases it through covers for a boundary.
Played to the point region by Che.
Pitched up again around off, Pujara gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Fullish delivery on the pads, flicked away through square leg for a brace.
No foot movement as he blocks this ball from within the crease.
Stays back and defends the ball off his back foot.
Pitches it up to Kohli around off. He gets behind the ball and bunts it down.
Virat Kohli is the next man in.

OUT! Broad gets his man to play and gets him to nick. Four previous balls which went away, Dhawan was happy to leave them alone. This one too is shaping away but he is tempted to fish at this. Broad serves this full on that fifth stump channel, Dhawan leans ahead to drive it but doesn't commit himself fully to it. Ends up getting a thick outside edge. The ball flies towards the cordon where Buttler dives to his left and takes a good low catch. Both the openers have been sent back by Broad. India still trail by 196 runs. Can England make further inroads?
Length again outside the off stump, Dhawan watches it go through to the keeper.
This one is too far to make Dhawan play at it.
Good from Broad. Good length ball around off, Dhawan comes forward to play it but misses the ball.
Dhawan chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Full length ball in the tight off stump channel, Pujara defends it with his bat and pad close together.
Nicely done! Too straight from Curran, flicked away neatly to deep square leg to rotate strike.

On a length, takes off with some extra bounce. Dhawan tries to tuck it away but is hit high on the pads. A polite inquiry from the Englishmen has not been answered. That was high and was going down leg too.
On a length outside off, leaving Dhawan. He doesn't fiddle with it.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. One run added to the total.
Outside off, Pujara plants his front foot across to allow it through.
On a length around off, moving away after landing. Dhawan allows it through.
Wide outside off, Shikhar leaves it alone.
Full ball outside off, eased nicely through covers for a couple.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Full ball outside off, Dhawan charges down the track. Don't know why he was doing so. Anyways, he doesn't fiddle with it. Sanity prevails.

Dhawan must have had his heart in his mouth! How did that miss the off stump? Broad has found out a way against Dhawan. This one lands on a good length, angling in initially and then moves away nicely after landing. Shikhar pushes at it but is beaten all ends up. The English players have their hands on their heads.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On a length on middle and leg, some nibble in the air. Pujara fails to defend it and is hit on the thigh pad. No real appeal for an LBW as it was heading down leg.
Curran brings out the bouncer surprisingly. Pujara is taken aback a touch but does well to sway away from the line and drops his wrists.
Short of a length on middle, tucked towards mid-wicket.
Continues to probe in the off stump channel, Cheteshwar brings his bat down late and blocks it.
Pitched up ball around off, Pujara keeps his bat and pad close together and defends it tentatively.

Safe! There is no inside edge! England are following in their opposition's footsteps and waste a review. Good length ball around off, straightens after landing. Dhawan tries to play it across and the ball goes off something behind. Cook at first slip takes it and appeals along with Broad. Kumar Dharmasena remains unmoved though. The English skipper gets into a meeting with some of his men and then decides to take the review. Snicko comes into play and there is clear daylight between bat and ball. The ball actually brushed the thigh pad of the batsman on its way through. The teams need to be sensible with the use of DRS.
Dhawan has been caught by Cook in the slip cordon. Was there an inside edge? England certainly feel so as Cook has a conversation with his teammates and challenges the decision.

Ooh! Much better from Broad. Lands this one in the corridor of uncertainty and gets the ball to nip away off the seam. Dhawan who is looking to leave it alone decides to put his bat down late. Is late anyway as the ball whizzes past his outside edge.
Fourth leave in a row. Wide outside off, shaping away. Dhawan lets it be.
Broad continues to bowl in the outside off stump channel. Shikhar watches it go past him.
Harmless ball on the fifth stump channel, not fiddled with.
On a length outside off, taking off with extra bounce and nipping away too. Dhawan points his bat skywards to allow it through.
Curran begins with a maiden. Good stuff from him. Brings this one back in late. Pujara leans ahead and dead-bats it.
Back of a length ball on off, Pujara hangs back and pushes at it but gets it off the outer half towards gully.
Pitched up ball outside off, jagging away with the natural left-armer's angle. Cheteshwar doesn't flirt with danger.
Pujara is playing late! He waits for this pitched up ball and taps it to covers.

There is a bit of a gap between Pujara's bat and pad when he is playing at deliveries. That will be encouraging for Curran. He lands this one outside off and gets it to shape in appreciably. CP comes ahead and keeps it out to the off side.
Starts off with a full length ball outside off, moves in late. Pujara covers his stumps and watches it sail through into the hands of the keeper.

Sam Curran comes into the attack. He was the hero for England in the first Test in Edgbaston. He was also the star with the bat in the previous innings. Can he put in a similar performance with the ball too?
Good length ball outside off, Dhawan knows where his off stump is and makes an assured leave.

FOUR! Pristine timing on that one! Full ball on middle and leg, Dhawan moves inside the line exposing his leg stump. He connects nicely with the flick as he plays it behind square leg. Rashid in the deep hares to his right but only comes second best. That one flew off the bat.
Harmless ball well outside off, third leave in a row by Dhawan.
Full ball swinging away, Dhawan plants his front foot across and doesn't fiddle with it.
In the zone outside off, Shikhar leaves it alone.

That could have gone anywhere! Back of a length ball attacking the rib-cage of the batsman. Dhawan tries to tuck it away but gets a leading edge. Broad in his followthrough stretches out his right hand but the ball lands safely.

Edged but safe! Pujara is not moving his feet in the correct manner. This time he camps back to a fullish ball around off. Pushes at it but ends up edging it behind. Luckily for him, it goes on the bounce to the second slip fielder. The soft hands saved him there.
Shortish ball, seaming in. CP camps back and presents a water-tight defense.
Fractionally overpitched on middle and leg, pushed off the front foot to mid on.
There is a slight field change. The man behind square leg comes a touch in front. He is placed at a catching position.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.

Oohs and Aahs from the Englishmen! Back of a length ball around off, coming in. Pujara instead of staying back comes ahead to deal with it. Misses to get hit above the knee roll. A casual appeal from Jimmy and Co but they bail out of it soon. Height was the factor there.
Full ball attacking the stumps, eased away through square leg for a single.
In the corridor outside off, shaping away. Cheteshwar lets it be. Consecutive maidens for Stuart Broad.
Pitched up ball just outside off, CP shuffles a touch and defends it down the track.
The batsman has been struck on the thigh pad.
Pujara is being put on pressure! Broad hits the deck hard and puts Pujara into an uncomfortable position. He tries to fend it off but the ball hits his bottom hand and lobs in front of square leg.
On a length outside off, CP plays it with an angled bat towards the point region.
Fullish ball around off, kept out watchfully.
Hangs back to the back of the length ball and defends it right under his eyes.

Anderson has got the better of Dhawan here! Bowls this one with a wobbly seam and lands it around off. The ball pitches and seams away. Dhawan pokes at it and misses. The thing that Dhawan did well was that he didn't follow the line of the ball or else he would have edged it.

Close shave! Certainly not where Dhawan intended it to go. Fullish ball around off, there is nibble in the air. Shikhar pushes at it gingerly and gets a thick inside edge that just goes past the leg stump to fine leg. A couple taken.
Fuller in length this time, jagging away. Shikhar doesn't flirt with it.
Shortish ball attacking the body of Dhawan. He rises with the bounce and stonewalls it besides the pitch.
Good length ball on middle and leg, Dhawan tries to keep it out but is hit on the thigh pad.
Not a convincing leave! Good length ball around off, moves away. Pujara bails out at the last moment as he drops his wrists. A wicket maiden for Anderson.
On a good length, defended solidly off the back foot.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Broad bowls a big inswinger first up to Pujara. He is late to bring his bat down and somehow keeps it out towards square leg. Stuart gives the batsman a smile and he smiles back. He knows that the pacer is trying to fox him.
Cheteshwar Pujara strides out to bat.

OUT! No, there is no surprise! A review goes down the drain for India. Stuart Broad has struck early this morning, just what the doctor ordered for England. He steams in from over the wicket and bowls a fuller length ball in the avenue of apprehension. After landing, the ball nips in appreciably. Rahul falls over a touch in an attempt to flick it across and misses. Is pinged on the pads and Broad rises up in a vociferous appeal. Umpire Kumar Dharmasena thinks about it and then raises his finger. The body language of KL suggests that he is not confident. Has a talk with his partner and reluctantly signals for the 'T'. Time for the replays. Snicko doesn't spot anything. Hawk Eye rolls in and displays three reds. The right-hander is on his way back. His woes around the off stump continue to haunt him.
Rahul has been trapped in front of the stumps but he still takes a chance with the review after having a chat with Dhawan. Are we in for a surprise?
Pitched up ball around off, kept out watchfully.

An appeal for an LBW is turned down! Fullish ball around leg stump, swinging down. Dhawan tries to flick it but misses to get pinged on the pads. The English players appeal but the umpire is not interested. Looked like it pitched outside leg.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.

There is enough movement for both Anderson and Broad but the batsmen have done well to score freely. Jimmy allows the ball to swing and brings it in appreciably. Rahul plays it off the inner half in front of square leg. A couple taken.

FOUR! Shot! That will make him feel confident. Back of a length ball around off, nips away after pitching. Rahul makes use of the depth of the crease and punches it through covers to pick up a boundary.

In the corridor of uncertainty, taking off after landing. Rahul points his bat upwards, keeps his eyes on the ball and makes a good leave. That is how a ball should be left, watching it till the very last moment.
That is beautifully bowled! Anderson runs in with good rhythm from over the wicket and bowls a fullish ball around off. It shapes in as Rahul leans ahead and dead-bats it.
Fourth dot in a row! This one is better. Closer to the off stump, the ball moves away late with some extra bounce. Dhawan watches it closely and makes a watchful leave.
In the same channel, the southpaw is in no mood to flirt with it.
Similar delivery, not close enough to make the batsman play. Shikhar remains circumspect in approach as he lets it pass.
Full ball outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Sweet Pitched up ball well outside off, Dhawan leans into it and caresses it through cover-point. The timing is spot on and the ball whistles away to the fence.

Tentative from Rahul! On a driveable length outside off, KL comes forward and pushes at it with hard hands but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball rolls towards the off side and the batsmen steal a run. He has been dismissed by chopping it on in this series. Needs to be careful.
Stuart Broad to bowl from the other end. Three slips and a gully in place for him.
Pretty harmless delivery on the fifth stump channel, Shikhar doesn't fiddle with it. 6 runs from the first over of this morning, good start for India.
In the channel outside off, leaving the southpaw. He lets it go.

Fractionally overpitched on the pads, Dhawan tickles it away through square leg. The fielder in the deep moves to his right to cut it off. Dhawan wants the third but he has been sent back by his partner.

FOUR! First runs of the morning! Well bowled and well played as well. Jimmy continues to probe in around off stump. Dhawan waits for it and opens the face of the bat at the last moment. He deliberately guides it past the slip cordon to find the fence.

The shiny side of the ball is on the outside, pointing towards the slip cordon. The ball moves away prodigiously around the off stump channel. Shikhar keeps his bat inside the line and makes a good leave.
Anderson starts off with a fuller length ball around off, as expected, he gets some nice away swing. Dhawan plants his front foot across to let it go.

We are set to get rolling. The men who matter come out to the middle. It is a terrific day for cricket as the sun is shining in all its glory. The Indian openers, Shikhar Dhawan and KL Rahul, will resume their innings. The legendary James Anderson is ready to steam in with the red cherry which is pretty fresh. Four slips in place. Here we go...

Sanjay Manjrekar doing the pitch report first says that there is no rain threat for a few more days. On looking down, he mentions that this Day 2 pitch has two changes. One is that the fast bowlers have hit the deck hard and have left some marks on the surface which he feels will assist in movement. The second thing he points out is that the rough is very close to the right-handed batsmen and it will help the spinners.

Hello and a warm welcome to the coverage of Day 2 of the Southampton Test. The visiting bowlers have ruled the roost to give their side the upper hand in this game. It is up to their batsmen now to back them up and take the game away from England. It won't be easy for them though as they are up against a penetrative pace bowling attack. It will be about being sensible and capitalizing on the match situations. The hosts, on the other hand, will still believe in themselves. If they make early inroads this morning, their confidence will receive a boost. Expect a tough tussle between bat and ball.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

The English all-rounder then stitched a breezy 63-run stand in 57 balls along with Stuart Broad which took the home side to a respectable total. Having said all this, India still hold the aces. Agreed that the ball is moving around but if you apply yourself, runs can be scored on this track. The first hour of the second day will be important from the point of view of both the sides. If England pick up a few quick wickets, it can lead to a collapse while India will know that if they bat well in the initial phase, they will further strengthen their position. Join us on Day 2 at 1100 Local (1000 GMT) to catch all the action. Till then, cheers!

The Englishmen were reeling at 86/6 but the pair of Moeen Ali and Sam Curran put in a rearguard effort. They put the bad balls away and kept the scoreboard ticking, adding 81 runs together in the process. India must have thought they can deflate the morale of the home side by bowling them out cheaply but the young Curran in particular shored things up for his team.

Safely Negotiated! The Indian openers, Shikhar Dhawan and KL Rahul have seen off the tricky phase (20-odd minutes) to head back unscathed to their dressing room. It has been a day which has been dominated by the Indian bowlers. When the ball was new, the trio of Jasprit Bumrah, Ishant Sharma and Mohammed Shami exploited it to perfection, breaking the backbone of the hosts.
Pitched up ball outside off, Rahul comes forward and lets it go to see off the day. THAT'S STUMPS ON DAY 1!
Full ball outside off, Dhawan pushes at it but squirts it off the outer half of the bat past gully. Three runs taken.
Tentative! On a length on middle and leg, Rahul is early into his flick and hence, gets a leading edge. It is safe though as the ball lands in the cover region. A single taken.

Four Byes! On a length outside off, KL Rahul leaves it alone. The ball swings away as Buttler dives to his right but it brushes his fingertips and rolls behind. Cook chases it and puts in a slide to keep the ball in play. It is checked upstairs. The replay shows that Cook's leg was in contact with the ropes when he had the ball in his hand.
Full ball around off, kept out watchfully.
FOUR! Streaky runs! On a length around off, Rahul plays it with soft hands but gets it off the outer half of the bat past the gap between the slip cordon and gully. Another boundary results.
Nicely done! On a length around off, Dhawan keeps his bat close to his body and blocks it.
That was sweet! Overpitched outside off, Rahul leans ahead and strokes it through covers. Three runs taken.
On a length around off, Rahul shuffles a touch and dead-bats it.
Third leave in a row! Anderson needs to make the batsmen play which he hasn't done so far. Well outside off, left alone.
In the zone outside off again, swinging away. Rahul doesn't flirt with danger.
In the fifth stump channel, KL Rahul plants his front foot across to allow it through.

Back of a length outside off, Rahul has a poke at it and gets it off the outer half past the slip cordon. Stokes and Bairstow are after it. The former slides near the fence and parries it to his mate. Good teamwork and they save a run for their side.
Wide! Way outside off, swinging away further. Rahul has nothing to do with it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Another one that has been slipped down the leg side, Lokesh fails to put bat on ball again.
Short but the line is wayward  but down the leg side, Rahul tries to flick it away but misses.

A chirpy appeal for an LBW is denied! Good length ball in the corridor of uncertainty, seams in a touch. Rahul camps back to defend it but misses to get hit above the knee roll. Broad is pleading for it along with the slip cordon but the umpire stays put. They don't go for the review. Rightly so, the replay shows it was too high.
Good length ball in the tight off stump corridor, Rahul hangs back and keeps it out down the track.
Stuart Broad to share the new ball from the other end.
Well played but not in the gap! Fractionally overpitched outside off, driven nicely to the man at point. Anderson begins with a maiden.
Anderson switches to around the wicket and bowls a full ball outside off. It moves away yet again and Dhawan has another easy leave to make.
No, this one swings away as well and Shikhar has no trouble in leaving it alone.
Full length ball on off, leaving the southpaw again. He leans ahead, keeps his bat inside the line and lets it pass. Is he setting Dhawan up for the big inswinger?
Well outside off, shaping away further. Shikhar doesn't fiddle with it.
Starts off with a length ball on off and it swings away sharply. Dhawan points his bat skywards to allow it through.
